transcript:
<meeting header>
Date: 2026-12-07
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Derek Huang (Redwood SE), Sara Novak (AegisCore), Jon Ruiz (AegisCore), Priya Menon (AegisCore)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, I'm Maya with Redwood Inference. Derek's here from solutions. Quick roll call?
[02:15] Sara Novak: Sara here, Head of Data Platform at AegisCore. Main goal today is to make sure SSO and security are clear before we kick off the pilot.
[05:12] Derek Huang: Great, we'll walk SAML details, what we need for IdP metadata, network and pilot metrics. We'll also flag common gotchas with ADFS and attribute mapping.
[07:40] Jon Ruiz: Real quick — we use ADFS as our IdP, SP-initiated flow required. We need ACS URL and entityID. Also interested in audit log retention and whether logs can be pushed to our S3.
[10:02] Maya Patel: We'll provide SP metadata and ACS/EntityID. We support pushing audit logs to customer S3 or accessing via API. Hosted default retention is 90 days but extended retention is available as an add-on.
[13:30] Priya Menon: For the pilot we need data residency in us-west-2 and PII masking for logs. Also we might evaluate Dedicated later if throughput looks high.
[16:05] Derek Huang: Residency is doable — we can pin Hosted workloads to us-west-2 for the pilot. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and lower tail latency but has procurement lead time. We'll cover the cost/latency delta.
[19:20] Sara Novak: Can you give us a ballpark for tail latency improvements on Dedicated vs Hosted? We care about P95 and P99.
[22:00] Derek Huang: Dedicated generally reduces variability and gives better P99; Hosted is usually fine for P95 in many cases. We'll run a baseline with your sample prompts to quantify. Expect a follow-up sheet with per-token costs and tail-latency numbers.
[25:30] Jon Ruiz: About SAML attributes — we need group mapping into RBAC and an 'environment' claim to distinguish dev/prod. Also, ADFS sometimes encrypts claims; that caused issues before.
[28:45] Maya Patel: We support attribute mapping. Our docs show examples for Okta and ADFS and we will include troubleshooting steps for encrypted claims and NameID formats — sometimes the sample docs call it 'teams' which is an older field name, heads-up.
[32:10] Priya Menon: On networking, what do we need to open? Our infra is very strict on outbound.
[35:00] Derek Huang: We'll provide the minimal CIDR ranges and ports for control plane and traffic egress plus recommended S3 endpoints for log push. For Private deployments there is no outbound egress requirement. We'll include an architectural diagram.
[38:20] Sara Novak: Security docs — can you supply SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest/in-transit details, and KMS integration notes? We need to run them through our compliance team.
[41:35] Maya Patel: Yes, we'll attach a redacted SOC 2, encryption whitepaper and KMS integration guide. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption; BYOK/HSM is supported for Dedicated/Private.
[45:00] Jon Ruiz: Key rotation and HSM — supported? We need rotation events surfaced to our audit log.
[48:15] Derek Huang: HSM via partner KMS is supported on Private; rotation can be scheduled and events are logged. We'll include examples of IAM policies and ARNs.
[51:40] Sara Novak: Pilot success criteria — propose: 1) SSO validated with 3 test users; 2) baseline of 200 req/min with P95 < 450ms; 3) no security blockers for control plane. Thoughts?
[55:10] Derek Huang: Those are reasonable. To hit 200 rpm at that latency we might recommend a small dedicated pool but can emulate on Hosted for the baseline. We'll prepare the pilot config and test harness.

[55:40] Maya Patel: Quick recap and owners — Maya: send SP metadata, SSO checklist and security pack by 2026-12-08; Jon: provide IdP metadata, cert and 3 test users by 2026-12-09; Derek: pilot config, k6/python scripts and cost/latency sheet by 2026-12-11. Pilot run 2026-12-14 to 12-16, review 2026-12-18.
[56:00] Sara Novak: We'll aim to meet those dates. Thanks for the clarity.
[56:10] Priya Menon: Thanks all.

<end transcript>
